exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
outcome: brain function status (hypoxia index, emotional resistance, sleep index, outside focus, brain fatigue, brain emptying, reaction speed, anxiety tendency, introverted brain, brain inhibition, brain stability, inner focus, oxygen deficiency index, brain coordination)
cohort: A total of 88 outpatient postpartum women with pelvic floor dysfunction, including 48 who had a cesarean section and 40 who had a vaginal delivery, were included in the study.
finding: Most postpartum women exhibited abnormal brain function across several domains, and these brain function problems were found to correlate with pelvic floor function and gestational weight gain.
mod_finding: Statistical differences were observed in brain fatigue and brain emptying between postpartum women who had vaginal delivery and those who had cesarean section.
